thread:
alexa: Pushing up Pioneer13b-int4 to canary, seeing intermittent OOMs during warmup when requests hit max_new_tokens > 256. Repro on 3/5 canary instances.

mike: Ugh, sounds like classic KV prefetch + frag. Any logs? :eyes:

jordan: Can you paste the exact payload or route config? Might be batch settings + slot reserve interacting.

alexa: Logs snippet: `oom: alloc failed 0x2000000 kv_prefetch slot_reserve=0.12 batch_size=8` — happens after a burst of long generations.

sam-bot: Canary deploy 3666660000 started by alexa. Instances: canary-3, canary-4, canary-5.

linda: Two quick mitigations: (1) lower default max_new_tokens to 256 for the canary route, (2) reduce slot_reserve to 0.06 temporarily. Both are quick toggles in route config.

alexa: Trying that now. Will flip max_new_tokens and push a soft throttle: `rbctl route update pioneer13b --max_new_tokens 256 --slot_reserve 0.06`

mike: Also try disabling KV prefetch on canary to confirm whether prefetching causes fragmentation spike: `prefetch: off` in model policy.

jordan: If disabling prefetch stabilizes, we can try a more surgical approach: enable prefetch but cap per-request prefetch bytes and enable lazy-kv-evict.

alexa: Quick test results: after setting max_new_tokens=256 + slot_reserve=0.06 and prefetch=off, no OOMs for ~20 minutes under the same load. Memory usage still has small jumps but no failures.

sam: Nice. But long-term we should root-cause fragmentation pattern. Could be the int4 quant kernel allocating transient buffers during attention with long seqs. We should run profiler on canary-4.

linda: Agreed. Plan: 1) keep soft defaults for canary for 24h; 2) run per-op memory trace on a repro node (capture slab allocs + KV churn); 3) try a conservative kernel fallback that avoids transient peak allocation.

mike: For step 2, use `memtrace` agent: `rbctl trace start canary-4 --filters=alloc,kv,slab --duration=120` then hit with ramp script.

jordan: Also add an eval to catch quality regression from int4 fallback: small eval set to run after any kernel change. We don't want to hurt perplexity.

alexa: Kicked off memtrace now. Ramp script running. If trace points to prefetch buffers, we can try selective prefetch (prefix-only).

sam-bot: Trace capture complete: /artifacts/3666660000/canary-4/memtrace-120.tar.gz

linda: Looking at trace — big contiguous allocations around step 84 correlated with `kv_prefetch_prepare`. That matches the earlier symptom.

mike: Ok next experiment: re-enable prefetch but add `prefetch_limit_bytes: 1MB` and `lazy_kv_eviction: true` in policy. Also bump microbatching to 16 to amortize overhead.

jordan: Microbatching to 16 might increase latency tails for single-request fast-path. Make it conditional: `batch_if_queue_time>10ms`.

alexa: Deploying policy patch now and will monitor:
```yaml
policy:
  prefetch: on
  prefetch_limit_bytes: 1048576
  lazy_kv_eviction: true
  microbatch: 16
  batch_condition: queue_time>10ms
```

linda: Rollout checklist: canary -> observe 1h -> if stable, promote to dedicated staging with slot_reserve 0.08 and max_new_tokens 320.

sam: Also add an automated alert for OOM spikes + a regression eval run when we bump kernel. I can add that to the rollout playbook.

alexa: For posterity, creating a short runbook note in the canary channel with the mitigation steps and the memtrace link. Will follow up with perf numbers after 1h. :thumbsup:

mike: Thanks — great triage. If we still see frag after the limit, next step is a small kernel change to avoid a double-buffer on attention. Jordan can lead the perf patch.

jordan: On it. Will prototype a fallback kernel that streams attention buffer and push a canary build tomorrow.

alexa: Update at +1h: new policy held, 0 OOMs, tail latency stable, small perf hit (~3% qps) but acceptable for now. We'll keep the staged defaults and schedule kernel work.

linda: Solid. Closing triage for now, leaving thread open for kernel patch progress.

sam: Noted. Thanks everyone.
